title: Hindu Temples: What Happened to Them, Vol. 2
byline: by Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · 1991 · subtitled The Islamic Evidence
lede: Volume 1 listed the sites. This volume sets out to prove the pattern from Islamic sources alone: mosque inscriptions that boast of replacing temples, a long survey of what Muslim chroniclers wrote, and a case study of the Rudramahalaya at Sidhpur in Gujarat. Then Goel traces the idea to its source, the destruction of pagan shrines in Arabia, and argues that iconoclasm follows from monotheist theology itself.

note: Goel argues from Muslim chronicles and inscriptions, which often exaggerate their rulers' zeal. Historians such as Richard Eaton read the same records as politics rather than doctrine. This page summarises Goel's evidence and argument, attributed to him.

sections.eyebrow: Appendix 1 · Muslim dynasties in India's history
sections.title: Who ruled, and when
sections.lede: The dynasties Goel lists, from the Caliphate to Tipu Sultan. Their periods overlap, and only the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals ruled most of the north.
items: From the “rightly-guided” caliphs to the Abbasids
sections.note: Dates are as given in the book's appendix. Colour shows the kind of power: northern empires, regional sultanates, Deccan sultanates, and outside powers.

sections.title: Twenty-one inscriptions, by century
sections.lede: Goel collects Persian and Arabic inscriptions on mosques that themselves record a temple's demolition or reuse, from the Quwwat al-Islam in Delhi to Cumbum in Andhra. The peak is the 17th century, Aurangzeb's reign.
items: Poonamallee, Udayagiri, Bodhan, Mathura, Gwalior, Akot, Bidar, Siruguppa, Cuddapah
sections.note: Grouped by Itihas from the dates in each entry. Several sites carry more than one inscription.

sections.title: The Rudramahalaya
sections.lede: A test case Goel builds from official documents: a Note from the Gujarat government, the Minorities Commission report, and an article by the archaeologist B.L. Nagarch.
items: Under Mularaja, the first Chaulukya king, according to Nagarch.
A central temple with eleven shrines to the Rudras.
By Ulugh Khan, Alauddin Khalji's general.
By Ahmad Shah of Gujarat. Shrines on the western side become a three-domed Jami Masjid.
The Minorities Commission takes up a complaint about the ASI's work there, which leads to this book's opening chapters.

sections.title: The gods of pre-Islamic Arabia
sections.lede: Goel describes the pagan Arabs as tolerant, honourable and devoted to many gods, and he lists the pantheon. He argues their fate under Islam foreshadowed India's.

sections.title: Shrines destroyed in Muhammad's lifetime
sections.lede: From the early biographies and histories (Ibn Ishaq, al-Tabari and others), as Goel compiles them. He treats this as the model later iconoclasts followed, the Sunnah.
